subject: Regulated data lifecycle: PII/PHI retention & redaction options
messages:
From: Claire Mendez <claire.mendez@medhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PII/PHI handling — retention limits & redaction options for Private deployment

Hi Stephanie,

We’re evaluating Redwood Private for a pilot that will process PHI extracted from our EHR feeds. Security has two quick asks before procurement: 1) maximum default data retention for request/response logs and embeddings for Private deployments, and 2) recommended approaches you support for redacting or tokenizing identifiers prior to long-term storage.

Specifically: can Redwood enforce a 30-day retention for any request/response payloads containing PHI by config (or automated lifecycle policy)? If not, what are your documented deletion timelines and mechanisms (API call + audit) for enforced deletion? Also, do you ship any built-in redaction helpers (PII/PHI classifiers, regex templates) or integrate with in-line tokenization partners?

We’ll need answers for our HIPAA assessment and to map to our BAA. Happy to set a short call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Mendez
Sr. Security Analyst — MedHealth Systems
secops@medhealth.com

--
MedHealth is evaluating two vendors in parallel; this is time-sensitive for our procurement timeline (target Jan 2027).

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Claire Mendez <claire.mendez@medhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PII/PHI handling — retention limits & redaction options for Private deployment

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’m looping Markus (legal/tech policy) and Grace (CS lead) to provide specifics and a short playbook. If useful, I can share a redaction matrix and sample lifecycle config by EOD.

1) Retention cap: For Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) you can configure retention at the route/model level. Out of the box we support retention policies down to 0 days (immediate deletion) and schedule-based purges (e.g., 30/90/365 days) via the lifecycle API; enforcement is local to the private control plane.

2) Deletion mechanisms & audit: Deletions can be performed via the Deletion API (single-record or bulk) and are recorded in the audit log with a SHA256 record id; for Private deployments with our optional audit connector we can stream deletion events to your SIEM. We will provide a reference playbook for generating attestation (time, actor, record ids).

3) Redaction/tokenization: We provide a lightweight PII classifier (name, ssn, mrn, dob, ccn patterns) that can run inline or as a preprocessor. For PHI-heavy workloads we recommend integrating an in-line tokenization partner (e.g., tokenization service / HSM-backed vault) — Redwood supports a pluggable preprocessor hook and has documented examples for two tokenization partners.

Markus — can you confirm the BAAs/contract language we typically provide, and Grace — can you attach the redaction matrix we discussed?

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your security and procurement next week if that helps.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0122

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:16:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PII/PHI handling — retention limits & redaction options for Private deployment

Stephanie / Grace — notes from legal/controls perspective for the playbook: 

- BAA & contract language: we provide a standard BAA that includes data controller/processor roles and explicit deletion SLA language. For Private deployments the customer retains control over data, but Redwood will operate the deletion APIs described in the BAA. Typical phrasing we propose: "Redwood will execute deletion requests within 30 calendar days and provide attestation logs within 5 business days of request completion." We can negotiate shorter windows depending on customer commitments and Dedicated capacity requirements.

- Retention enforcement: emphasize that for Private customers the retention policy is a config in the control plane. We should capture implementation details: lifecycle policy key (retention_days), cron-based purge job id, and audit entry format.

- Redaction recommendations: prefer pre-ingest tokenization for direct identifiers (SSN, MRN, full DOB) and redaction/differential masking for less-sensitive fields. If MedHealth requires in-transit redaction prior to any transient KV cache writes, call that out — we support prefix-based caching controls and can disable KV persistence for specific routes.

I’m attaching a redaction matrix (field -> recommended action -> max retention) and a short clause template for the BAA.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx, MA-for-data-lifecycle.docx

Stephanie / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. A few follow-ups:

- Can you confirm the deletion attestation format? We need: request id, timestamp, actor, sha256 of deleted payload, and a link to the audit entry or export.
- Is the redaction classifier you referenced open-source or closed? We prefer solutions we control; if it’s closed we’ll need to run a validation test.
- Procurement asks for a BAA-ready DocuSign; can you provide the naming convention and an expected turnaround for countersign (we try to close vendor BAAs within 10 business days).

If the technical sync can include a brief demo of the lifecycle API and a quick run-through of the redaction classifier accuracy on a small sample, that would be ideal.

Claire
